items.q: Our auditor expects stainless. Will PP pass?
items.a: No rule requires stainless steel. US and Canadian GMP (21 CFR 211.65, GUI-0001) ask for surfaces that do not react, add or absorb, and that survive sanitizing. Your qualification decides.

No water system is. USP sets limits for water, not approvals for equipment. The factory acceptance test (FAT) proves function before shipping. The site acceptance test (SAT) and operational qualification (OQ) prove it on your feed water.

items.q: Which edition of each standard do you design to?
items.a: The edition in force when you approve the functional specification. If a standard changes mid-project, we assess it under change control. We name the documents it touches; you approve the change.

items.q: Who registers our pressure equipment, and when?
items.a: The safety authority of each province where the item is used, before it is built. Each pressure-rated item needs a Canadian registration number (CRN) under CSA B51, unless exempt. Your proposal says how registration is handled.
